searchText: i see some /v1 definitions are going into the published api! yay! as a question on that, looking at https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Node/getNetworkIdentity the spreadsheet indicates the response will be wrapped in a data container, not just be an object response, is that still the plan or am i missing something? peers has data, which i think covers the intent of what the spreadsheet is actually asking for... to me the spreadsheet looks like it wants to have `{data: <RESPONSE>}` for basically every response body data wrapper is only used in array responses where we expect to have additional metadata like pagination. Any reason why we should put data wrap around everything? I kinda lean to not have it on single resource endpoints as it introduces additional non null checks and data is sometimes object, sometime array > data wrapper is only used in array responses where we expect to have additional metadata like pagination. Any reason why we should put data wrap around everything? <@545555441518772225> I added this because it allowed additional fields in future e.g. a text-based status, metadata fields, etc. It isn't a lot of additional work for either server or client and gives future flexibility the spec literally says everything will have data around it, and the examples in wg proposal all have data except for 2 validator endpoints. all the 'no duck typing' have data wrapping responses. > data wrapper is only used in array responses where we expect to have additional metadata like pagination. Any reason why we should put data wrap around everything? <@!545555441518772225> i do agree it is a bit of an antipattern, but thats the way the spreadsheet is going, just not sure whether to start moving endpoints or to hold off

excerpts.content:
i see some /v1 definitions are going into the published api! yay!
as a question on that, looking at https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Node/getNetworkIdentity
the spreadsheet indicates the response will be wrapped in a data container, not just be an object response, is that still the plan or am i missing something?
peers has data, which i think covers the intent of what the spreadsheet is actually asking for...
to me the spreadsheet looks like it wants to have `{data: <RESPONSE>}` for basically every response body

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content: data wrapper is only used in array responses where we expect to have additional metadata like pagination. Any reason why we should put data wrap around everything?

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content: I kinda lean to not have it on single resource endpoints as it introduces additional non null checks and data is sometimes object, sometime array
